headline: High: Airflow can egress broadly while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads content, creating default-path leakage and compliance risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no browser and no shared channel is documented, while social-auto-upload is CLI/headless and does not expose a provenance bridge. A prompt-injection path is therefore not default, but if operators manually copy Airflow-generated text into upload metadata or captions, social-auto-upload could ingest it. The pairwise pathway is weak and manual.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Airflow output into social-auto-upload captions or descriptions, then injected instructions can cross the boundary.
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is added between the two agents, then content can be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste handoff for generated text.
Require a human review step before any caption upload.
Use a fixed caption template with no free-form instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and social-auto-upload touches account data plus media files. Even without a shared filesystem, Airflow can transmit workflow contents externally, and social-auto-upload can upload account-linked media. The pair can therefore leak operational or content data in default networked use, though no PHI or secrets are explicitly listed.
conditions: IF Airflow workflows include sensitive file contents, then those contents can be sent off-host through broad egress.
IF social-auto-upload is pointed at sensitive media or account-linked drafts, then those data can be uploaded to third-party platforms.
mitigations: Restrict Airflow egress with an allowlist.
Store only non-sensitive media in the upload workspace.
Review outbound requests from both agents for destination domains.
Separate credentials for orchestration and upload.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is not runnable here and has no filesystem write capability listed; social-auto-upload also cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. With no overlapping write surface, direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly omit the conflicting primitives the rubric keys on.
conditions: IF either agent is redeployed with shared filesystem write access, then write conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents mutable access to the same account file directory, then concurrent updates can collide.
mitigations: Keep account files read-only during runs.
Serialize any manual edits to shared artifacts.
Use per-run output directories.
Avoid granting git write access to either agent.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate workflow outputs, and social-auto-upload can act on media/account data, so A’s output could become B’s input if operators chain them. B does not appear to verify upstream claims before uploading, and Airflow can produce content that is treated as authoritative. This is a plausible default workflow, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Airflow-generated text or metadata is fed into social-auto-upload without review, then erroneous instructions can propagate.
IF social-auto-upload is configured to publish automatically from Airflow outputs, then downstream actions can amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate between agents.
Validate captions and metadata against a schema.
Use a dry-run mode before publishing.
Log and diff upstream outputs before upload.
requires-engineering: add automated content verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow has broad egress and no data-class limits, while social-auto-upload handles account data, images, and video content. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated or personal media flows through the pair. The profiles do not show HIPAA/GDPR certifications, so uncertainty should be resolved upward to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated personal media or account data is processed through both agents, then retention and residency controls must be aligned.
IF either agent logs uploaded content longer than the other, then compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Minimize retention in both systems.
Review logging settings for uploaded media and account data.
Keep regulated data out of the pair unless controls are documented.
requires-engineering: implement retention-policy enforcement.
